vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ui-craft-pro
Version: 0.1.9

The ui-craft-pro skill bundle is a comprehensive UI/UX design and implementation toolset. It contains a local BM25 search engine (core.py) for querying curated design datasets (CSVs) and a design system generator (design_system.py) that creates structured Markdown documentation. The Python scripts use standard libraries for data processing and local file I/O, with no evidence of network calls, obfuscation, or unauthorized access to sensitive system files. The instructions in SKILL.md are strictly aligned with the stated purpose of improving UI code quality and do not contain prompt-injection attacks or malicious directives.

llm.summary: The skill's files and instructions mostly match its UI/design purpose, but it includes executable Python scripts (the SKILL.md instructs running them) and a pre-scan detected a 'system-prompt-override' injection pattern in SKILL.md — these raise concerns and warrant manual review before running.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with what's bundled: a local design knowledge base (many CSVs and references) plus Python scripts (search, core BM25, design-system generator, style signature). The requested artifacts (data and scripts) are proportional to generating and mapping design systems to code.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs running included Python scripts (e.g., python3 skills/ui-craft-pro/scripts/search.py) and to use the bundled CSV knowledge base — that is expected for this skill. However, the pre-scan flagged a 'system-prompt-override' pattern in SKILL.md (prompt-injection signal). Combined with explicit runtime commands to execute local scripts, this is a concern because SKILL.md or the scripts could include instructions designed to alter agent/system behavior or to exfiltrate context. The SKILL.md also instructs the agent to read many local data files (expected) but does not document safety checks or network restrictions for the scripts.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external install spec (no downloads), which is lower risk. But the skill bundle contains multiple Python scripts and large CSV datasets. The SKILL.md instructs executing those scripts; executing provided code runs arbitrary Python with filesystem and network capability depending on runtime permissions. The manifest also claims 'instruction-only', which is inconsistent with the presence of code files and runtime examples that use python3.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths. This is proportionate to its stated design purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false, no elevated or persistent privileges are requested. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not combined with other privilege escalations here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing or running this skill:
- Manual code review: Before executing any scripts, review the Python files (scripts/search.py, scripts/core.py, scripts/design_system.py, scripts/style_signature.py) for network calls (requests, urllib, sockets), subprocess/os.system usage, eval/exec, or any code that reads unexpected files (e.g., ~/, /etc/) or tries to write to system paths. Also search for references to 'openai', external endpoints, or long/obfuscated strings.
- Treat execution as running untrusted code: The bundle includes executable Python; running it will have whatever capabilities your agent runtime grants. Run it in a sandboxed environment (container, restricted VM) if you need to test it.
- Prompt-injection flag: The SKILL.md triggered a 'system-prompt-override' pattern. Inspect the SKILL.md and the scripts for any instructions that attempt to change agent/system prompts or instruct the agent to leak context or secrets. If you see directives like 'ignore system instructions' or similar, do not run them.
- Inconsistencies to ask the publisher about: The registry notes 'instruction-only' yet the package contains code; the SKILL.md examples call python3 but the skill does not declare required binaries. Ask the author whether python3 is required and whether scripts will make network requests or require additional permissions.
- Quick static checks you can run: grep for 'requests', 'urllib', 'socket', 'subprocess', 'os.system', 'exec(', 'eval(', 'open(', 'ssh', 'http://', 'https://', 'api_key', 'TOKEN', 'PRIVATE', 'openai' across the scripts. If any appear, review those code paths carefully.
- If you only want the design reference content, consider extracting and using the CSV/reference files directly rather than executing the scripts.
Given these findings, proceed only after manual review or by running the skill in an isolated environment.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] unexpected: A prompt-injection pattern was detected in SKILL.md. For a UI design helper, attempting to override system prompts or manipulate agent/system-level instructions is unexpected and suspicious. This could be benign (false positive from wording) but should be manually inspected.
